title: He used to be happy among his people.
subtitle: Light joy, long grief
then: Ibn Kathir says he was happy and {trap}did not think about the consequences, nor feared what was in front of him. His light happiness will be followed by long grief.{/trap} Compare verse 9, where the other man returns to his family happy.
now: Weekends of fun, a busy social feed, the house full of laughter. {idea}Happiness is not the problem.{/idea} {trap}Being happy and never once thinking about the end is.{/trap}
old: As long as I am happy now, I am doing fine.
new: Joy is a gift, but joy that forgets the end can turn into grief.
try: In a happy moment today, say alhamdulillah and remember Who gave it.

title: He thought he would never return.
subtitle: The belief behind the careless life
then: Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said he believed he would not return to Allah, and {trap}that Allah would not bring him back after death{/trap}. The introduction calls this the misunderstanding that led to his fate.
now: Moving abroad and thinking, "I will never see these people again," so it does not matter how you left things. {idea}Every relationship has a return trip.{/idea}
old: Once I leave this life, nothing I did will follow me.
new: I will return to Allah, and what I did returns with me.
try: Fix one thing today you would not want to return to.

title: Yes he will. His Lord was always watching him.
subtitle: The answer to I will never return
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah will repeat his creation just as He began it{/idea}, and reward him by his deeds, good or bad. He was always watching, All-Knowing and All-Aware.
now: You assume no one noticed you helping the old man with his bags, or snapping at the delivery driver. {idea}Both were seen.{/idea} {reward}That is a warning and a comfort.{/reward}
old: Most of what I do goes unseen.
new: My Lord sees all of it, the good I hid included.
try: Do one kindness today that only Allah will see.

title: I swear by the red glow after sunset.
subtitle: The light that lingers before night
then: Scholars said Ash-Shafaq is the redness on the horizon between Maghrib and Isha. The introduction explains the oath: moving from this life to the Hereafter is {idea}as certain as twilight after sunset{/idea}.
now: You notice the red sky driving home and know night is close. {idea}You never doubt it.{/idea} The verse asks you to be that sure about what comes after this life.
old: What happens after death is uncertain and far away.
new: The Hereafter follows this life as surely as twilight follows sunset.
try: Watch the sky after sunset today and let it remind you of what comes next.

title: And by the night and all it gathers home.
subtitle: Night draws everything back
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said it means what the night gathers. Qatadah said stars and animals. Ikrimah said {idea}when it is night, everything goes to its home{/idea}.
now: Evening comes and the roads fill with people heading home, birds settle in trees, phones light up with "on my way." {idea}Every night rehearses a bigger return.{/idea}
old: Going home each night is just routine.
new: Each night, everything returning home reminds me I am returning too.
try: When you get home tonight, pause at the door and remember your final return.

title: And by the moon when it grows full.
subtitle: A cycle that completes
then: Ibn Abbas said it means when it comes together and becomes complete. {idea}Qatadah said when it completes its cycle.{/idea} The oath leads straight into the next verse about stages.
now: You see the full moon over the car park after a late shift. {idea}It got there one night at a time.{/idea} Your life is moving through its phases the same way.
old: My life is just random ups and downs.
new: Like the moon, my life moves through stages toward completion.
try: Look for the moon tonight and think about what stage of life you are in.

title: You will surely ride from stage to stage.
subtitle: Every state you are in will change
then: Ikrimah said: weaned after nursing, old after young. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: {idea}ease after difficulty, difficulty after ease, wealth after poverty, health after sickness{/idea}.
now: The hospital corridor at 3 a.m. The first month of the new job. The empty bank account before payday. {reward}None of these is permanent.{/reward} {idea}Neither is the good week.{/idea}
old: The way things are right now is how they will stay.
new: I am passing through stages, so I stay patient in hard ones and grateful in good ones.
try: Name the stage you are in. Write one thing to be patient with and one to be grateful for.

title: So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?
subtitle: After all these signs, a question
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: {idea}what prevents them from believing in Allah, His Messenger ﷺ and the Last Day?{/idea} The signs were in their own sky and their own lives.
now: You have lived through illness and recovery, broke months and good ones, seen babies born and grandparents buried. {idea}Ask yourself honestly what still holds you back.{/idea}
old: If I had clearer proof, I would be more committed.
new: The signs are already all around me. The question is what I do with them.
try: Write down one sign of Allah you saw today in your own life.

title: When the Quran is recited, they do not bow down.
subtitle: A verse of prostration
then: Ibn Kathir asks what is wrong with them that when Allah's words are recited, {idea}they do not prostrate out of awe, respect and reverence{/idea}. Abu Hurayrah prostrated at this surah, following the Prophet ﷺ.
now: The Quran plays in the car or on a phone while you scroll and chat. {idea}When did a verse last bring your head down?{/idea}
old: Listening to the Quran in the background is enough.
new: The Quran deserves my whole attention, even my forehead on the ground.
try: Listen to one short surah today with full attention, then make one sajdah of thanks.

title: Rather, those who disbelieve keep on denying.
subtitle: When denial becomes a habit
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}rejection, obstinacy and opposition to the truth{/trap} had become their way. It was not a lack of signs. It was a habit of saying no.
now: Someone gives you good advice and your reply is "yes, but" before they finish. {idea}Watch for that reflex in yourself.{/idea}
old: I push back because I am thinking critically.
new: Sometimes my pushback is just a habit of refusing what I do not want to hear.
try: Next time someone gives you advice today, listen to the end before replying.

title: Allah knows best what they keep inside.
subtitle: The heart behind the words
then: Mujahid and Qatadah both said it means {idea}what they conceal in their chests{/idea}. The deniers hid their real reasons, but nothing was hidden from Allah.
now: You tell friends you skipped the gathering because you were tired. {idea}Inside, it was jealousy.{/idea} Allah knows the real reason, and that is where change starts.
old: My private motives are my own business.
new: Allah knows what is inside me better than I do, so I can be honest with Him.
try: Ask yourself the real reason behind one choice you made today. Tell Allah honestly.

title: So give them news of a painful punishment.
subtitle: A warning delivered plainly
then: Ibn Kathir says it means: inform them, O Muhammad ﷺ, that {trap}Allah has prepared a painful torment for them{/trap}. Right after it, the surah opens an exception.
now: A friend tells you hard news about your health so you get treated in time. {reward}A plain warning is a kindness.{/reward} Let it reach your own habits first.
old: Warnings in the Quran are about other people.
new: The warning is for me first, and it comes with a door right beside it.
try: Let one verse of warning today lead you to one concrete change.

title: Except those who believe and do good: a reward that never ends.
subtitle: Faith in the heart, good in the hands
then: Ibn Kathir says belief is in the heart and righteous deeds are done with the limbs. Ibn Abbas said the reward is {reward}without being decreased{/reward}; Mujahid said without measure. He compares it to {reward}a gift without an end{/reward}.
now: The contract ends, the bonus is spent, the pension runs out. {idea}Every reward you know has a last payment.{/idea} This one has none.
old: Every good thing in life eventually runs out.
new: Faith joined with good deeds earns a reward that never stops.
try: Pair one belief with one action today: if you believe in charity, give a little.
